nodes.statement: It is possible to write a program that, when compiled and executed, outputs an exact copy of its own source code.
nodes.span: produce as output an exact copy of its source.
nodes.status_reason: reader can verify by attempting the programming exercise

nodes.statement: Figure 1 demonstrates a self-reproducing program written in C.
nodes.span: Figure 1 shows a self-reproducing program in the C programming language.
nodes.status_reason: reader can inspect the referenced figure

nodes.statement: A self-reproducing program can easily be generated by another program.
nodes.span: This program can be easily written by another program.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the definition of a self-reproducing program

nodes.statement: A self-reproducing program can include arbitrary additional code that will also be reproduced.
nodes.span: contain an arbitrary amount of excess baggage that will be reproduced
nodes.status_reason: follows from the structure of a self-reproducing program

nodes.statement: The C compiler is itself written in the C programming language.
nodes.span: The C compiler is written in C.
nodes.status_reason: factual statement about the C compiler

nodes.statement: The C compiler contains code that interprets character escape sequences in a portable way.
nodes.span: code in the C compiler that interprets the character escape sequence.
nodes.status_reason: factual statement about the C compiler's code

nodes.statement: Because the compiler can interpret escape sequences, it can recompile itself and perpetuate this ability.
nodes.span: allows it to recompile itself, thus perpetuating the knowledge.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the compiler being written in C

nodes.statement: To add a new escape sequence like "\v" to the compiler, one must first modify the compiler source to recognize it.
nodes.span: alter the C compiler to include the sequence "\v"
nodes.status_reason: hypothetical method step

nodes.statement: The compiler must be trained by temporarily using the decimal value of the new character so the old compiler can compile it.
nodes.span: We must "train" the compiler.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the compiler not initially knowing the new sequence

nodes.statement: Once the trained binary is installed as the official compiler, the portable version of the escape sequence can be used in the source.
nodes.span: install the resulting binary as the new official C compiler
nodes.status_reason: follows from successfully compiling the new sequence

nodes.statement: A compiler can learn a self-referencing definition after being trained once.
nodes.span: tell it once, then you can use this self-referencing definition.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the successful training of the compiler

nodes.statement: The compiler can be modified to deliberately miscompile source code when it matches a specific pattern, acting as a Trojan horse.
nodes.span: deliberately miscompile source whenever a particular pattern is matched.
nodes.status_reason: reader can inspect Figure 6

nodes.statement: A bug was planted in the compiler to match the UNIX login command.
nodes.span: bug I planted in the compiler would match code in the UNIX "login" command.
nodes.status_reason: historical account provided by the author

nodes.statement: The modified compiler altered the login command to accept a specific known password in addition to the normal one.
nodes.span: accept either the intended encrypted password or a particular known password.
nodes.status_reason: historical account provided by the author

nodes.statement: Installing this modified compiler binary allows the creator to log into the system as any user.
nodes.span: I could log into that system as any user.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the modified login command accepting a known password

nodes.statement: A blatant Trojan horse in the compiler's source code would be easily detected by reviewing the source.
nodes.span: casual perusal of the source of the C compiler would raise suspicions.
nodes.status_reason: follows from standard code review practices held by the reader

nodes.statement: A second Trojan horse is added to the compiler to hide the first one.
nodes.span: adds a second Trojan horse to the one that already exists.
nodes.status_reason: reader can inspect Figure 7

nodes.statement: The second Trojan horse uses a self-reproducing program to insert both Trojan horses into any newly compiled compiler.
nodes.span: self-reproducing program that inserts both Trojan horses into the compiler.
nodes.status_reason: reader can inspect Figure 7

nodes.statement: Inserting the self-reproducing Trojan horse requires a learning phase to train the compiler.
nodes.span: requires a learning phase as in the Stage II example.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the compiler bootstrapping process demonstrated in Stage II

nodes.statement: The modified source is compiled with a normal compiler to create a bugged binary, which is then installed as the official compiler.
nodes.span: compile the modified source with the normal C compiler to produce a bugged binary.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the learning phase method

nodes.statement: The Trojan horse code can then be removed from the compiler's source code, but the bugged binary will reinsert it during future compilations.
nodes.span: remove the bugs from the source of the compiler and the new binary will reinsert the bugs
nodes.status_reason: follows from the installed bugged binary recompiling the clean source

nodes.statement: As a result, the login command remains compromised without any trace of the malicious code in any source files.
nodes.span: login command will remain bugged with no trace in source anywhere.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the bugged binary hiding the Trojan horse

nodes.statement: Code cannot be trusted unless it was entirely created by the user.
nodes.span: You can't trust code that you did not totally create yourself.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the demonstration of an undetectable Trojan horse

nodes.statement: Source-level verification is insufficient to protect against untrusted code.
nodes.span: No amount of source-level verification or scrutiny will protect you
nodes.status_reason: follows from the demonstration of an undetectable Trojan horse

nodes.statement: This type of attack can be implemented in any program-handling software or hardware microcode, not just C compilers.
nodes.span: could have picked on any program-handling program such as an assembler
nodes.status_reason: follows from the generalizability of the compiler attack

nodes.statement: Trojan horses become increasingly difficult to detect when placed in lower-level programs.
nodes.span: As the level of program gets lower, these bugs will be harder and harder to detect.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the increased opacity of lower-level programs

nodes.statement: The actions of computer hackers are equivalent to vandalism, trespass, and theft.

nodes.statement: Breaking into a computer system should carry the same social stigma as breaking into a physical house.

nodes.statement: The press should treat computer misuse as a dangerous and mundane crime, similar to drunk driving.
